quotes.quote: Following stringent quality filtering, we identified a total of 4157 amplicon sequence variants (ASVs) from 24 samples, using a 100% sequence similarity threshold.
Microbiome bioinformatics was performed with QIIME 2 2019.4 with slight modifications according to the official tutorials ( https://docs.qiime2.org/2019.4/tutorials/ ).

G1.rationale: The principal result includes a computational count of ASVs from 16S sequencing data, re-runnable by a third party using deposited data and QIIME 2.

quotes.quote: Following stringent quality filtering, we identified a total of 4157 amplicon sequence variants (ASVs) from 24 samples, using a 100% sequence similarity threshold.

G2.rationale: A primary numerical endpoint (total ASVs) is explicitly stated in the Results, making it identifiable.

quotes.quote: Microbiomics data sets were deposited at Mendeley Data under the DOI 10.17632/v8tx42gchw.1 ( https://data.mendeley.com/datasets/v8tx42gchw/1 ).
RNA-Seq data sets were deposited into the NCBI GEO under the accession number GSE271034 .

G3.rationale: The deposit listing shows only GSE271034 (RNA-Seq), but the target ASV count comes from microbiomics data deposited at Mendeley Data, which is not in the listing; thus the listed files are not the inputs for this target.

quotes.quote: Microbiome bioinformatics was performed with QIIME 2 2019.4 with slight modifications according to the official tutorials ( https://docs.qiime2.org/2019.4/tutorials/ ).
Sequences were then quality filtered, denoised, merged and chimera removed using the DADA2 plugin. Non-singleton ASVs were aligned with mafft and used to construct a phylogeny with fasttree2.

G4.rationale: The method for ASV calling is described with software versions and steps, sufficient to implement without original code.

quotes.quote: Microbiome bioinformatics was performed with QIIME 2 2019.4 with slight modifications according to the official tutorials ( https://docs.qiime2.org/2019.4/tutorials/ ).
